chunks: Yunus narrated from Ali ibn Salim, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: 'My father gave three bequests; which of them should I follow?' He said, 'Follow the last of them.' I said, 'Because they are fewer (in number/weight)?' He said, 'Even if they are few.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (a title for Imam al-Rida)

ai.seo_question: Which of multiple bequests should be followed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from the chapter on modifying wills, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) advises the narrator to prioritize the final of his father's three bequests, illustrating the principle of 'Akhira' (the last mentioned) in Shia jurisprudence. This guidance underscores that the validity or precedence of a bequest is not contingent upon its material magnitude but on its specific divine or legal standing, even if it seems minor. The narration highlights the scholarly nuance that a smaller, explicitly designated bequest may carry greater weight than larger ones if it represents the final intent or a specific obligation.
